why_angle: The rival pages (itechguides, stayingconnectedabroad, racksandwatts, sekin.in) and GL.iNet's cited product pages give only GL.iNet's maximum VPN figures. None gives a named reviewer's measured VPN speed or power draw. This page puts measured speed and power next to the ratings. In those tests the Beryl 7 got close to its OpenVPN rating (about 1,000 Mbps), while the Slate 7 managed about 100 Mbps against its 385 Mbps OpenVPN-DCO rating. It also explains why OpenVPN speed matters on hotel networks that block WireGuard's UDP traffic.

page.title: Best travel router with VPN for hotels (2026): WireGuard speed and hotel login pages
page.h1: Best travel router with VPN for hotels (2026)
page.desc: Which travel router with VPN holds up on hotel Wi-Fi: reviewer-measured WireGuard and OpenVPN speeds and power draw for the GL.iNet Beryl 7, Beryl AX, Slate 7 and Slate AX, priced at GL.iNet's US store on 2026-11-08.
page.answer: Short answer. The best travel router with VPN for hotels is the GL.iNet Beryl 7, which runs one WireGuard or OpenVPN tunnel for every device behind it. NASCompares measured its OpenVPN close to 1,000 Mbps and WireGuard approaching the 1,100 Mbps rating.

cells.tested: OpenVPN-DCO close to 1,000 Mbps; WireGuard approached 1,100 Mbps over Ethernet (NASCompares)
About 300 Mbps WireGuard, 116 Mbps OpenVPN (The Gadgeteer)
About 540 Mbps WireGuard; OpenVPN tops out around 100 Mbps (Mighty Gadget)
GL.iNet's own 2022 pre-launch test only: 550 Mbps WireGuard, 120 Mbps OpenVPN

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Price per Mbps of WireGuard rating: Beryl 7 $129.99 ÷ 1,100 = $0.12; Slate AX $119.99 ÷ 550 = $0.22; Slate 7 $159.99 ÷ 490 = $0.33; Beryl AX $98.99 ÷ 300 = $0.33. Per Mbps, the Beryl 7 costs about a third as much as the Beryl AX or Slate 7.
  • Measured OpenVPN gap: about 1,000 Mbps on the Beryl 7 (NASCompares) ÷ about 100 Mbps on the Slate 7 (Mighty Gadget) = about 10×, and the Beryl 7 costs $30 less.
  • Beryl AX against its own rating: on OpenVPN, The Gadgeteer measured 116 of the rated 150 Mbps (116 ÷ 150 = 77%). Its WireGuard result, about 300 Mbps, matched the rating.
  • Power on the road: NASCompares measured the Beryl 7 at 3.7–3.8 W while streaming 4K to three clients. Mighty Gadget measured the Slate 7 at 7–8 W in typical use, so the Beryl 7 draws about half as much. At 3.75 W, 10 Wh ÷ 3.75 W ≈ 2.7 h of Beryl 7 runtime for every 10 Wh a power bank delivers.
  • Distance to your VPN server: in one GL.iNet case, a traveler at 288 ms ping got 47.3 Mbps through WireGuard against 455 Mbps without the VPN (47.3 ÷ 455 = 10%). On long-haul trips, latency sets the speed, not the router's chip.

Measured VPN speeds, and why hotels can force OpenVPN

WireGuard runs over UDP only. The WireGuard project says it "explicitly does not support tunneling over TCP". OpenVPN's comparison page notes that firewalls blocking unknown UDP traffic also block WireGuard, and that OpenVPN can fall back to TCP port 443. On GL.iNet firmware 4, you set up that fallback by uploading your VPN provider's TCP .ovpn file. GL.iNet's docs quote CyberGhost that TCP is "a bit slower" than UDP. Download the TCP config before you travel. The OpenVPN figures below are upper limits for that fallback. Expect OpenVPN over TCP to run slower.

  • Beryl 7: NASCompares (Rob Andrews, February 2026) measured OpenVPN-DCO "close to 1000Mbps over Ethernet" and WireGuard that "approached the advertised 1100Mbps ceiling under favorable conditions". VPN traffic ran 20–25% below non-VPN traffic. The router reached a public Wi-Fi captive portal (the hotel login page) about 35 s after start-up, booted in about 51 s and switched between internet sources in 4–5 s. The case measured 41–42 °C after an hour of streaming. {buy:glinet-beryl-7-gl-mt3600be}
  • Beryl AX: The Gadgeteer (Joe Porletto, 2023) got WireGuard speeds "closer to 300Mbps" and 116 Mbps on OpenVPN over a month of use. The review doesn't state the test server or line speed. {buy:glinet-beryl-ax-gl-mt3000}
  • Slate 7: Mighty Gadget (James Smythe, 2026) measured about 540 Mbps on WireGuard, above the 490 Mbps rating. It says OpenVPN "tops out around 100Mbps", about a quarter of the 385 Mbps OpenVPN-DCO rating (100 ÷ 385 = 26%). A GL.iNet forum owner (bigbang) measured about 500 Mbps WireGuard in a local wired test. On this router, use WireGuard.
  • Slate AX: its only VPN figures come from GL.iNet's own 2022 pre-launch test: up to 550 Mbps WireGuard and 120 Mbps OpenVPN.

Power for the Beryl 7: it runs on USB-C PD. A GL.iNet staff member (will.qiu) warned on GL.iNet's forum that with only 5 V/3 A it "may not function properly". Use a charger or power bank port that supplies 9 V/3 A (27 W) or 12 V/2.5 A (30 W).

Not recommended

GL.iNet Slate AX (GL-AXT1800). At GL.iNet's US store it costs $10 less than the Beryl 7. For that it has half the WireGuard rating (550 vs 1,100 Mbps) and about an eighth of the OpenVPN rating (1,000 ÷ 120 = 8.3×), on older Wi-Fi 6, and its only VPN figures are the maker's 2022 pre-launch test.
